_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as detected by an FDA approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human, dose escalation and multicohort expansion study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC (114 in primary analysis: 27 treatment-naive and 87 previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) and duration of response
pivotal_trials.result: In treatment-naive patients, confirmed ORR 70% (95% CI 50, 86) with median DOR 9.0 months (95% CI 6.3, NE). In previously platinum-treated patients, confirmed ORR 57% (95% CI 46, 68) with median DOR not estimable (95% CI 15.2, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=25%): fatigue, constipation, musculoskeletal pain, and hypertension. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 5%. Permanent discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 15% of patients (pneumonitis 1.8%, pneumonia 1.8%, sepsis 1%).
target_moa: Pralsetinib is an orally bioavailable kinase inhibitor that targets the rearranged during transfection (RET) receptor tyrosine kinase; RET gene fusions are oncogenic drivers in NSCLC.

rems.type: No REMS required; no significant safety concerns identified during NDA review warranting a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).

companion_dx_detail: Oncomine Dx Target Test (ODxTT) to detect RET gene fusions; patients are selected based on the presence of a RET gene fusion.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; it was not deemed necessary as no review issues raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to regular approval for adult patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the conversion from accelerated to regular approval of GAVRETO for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic rearranged during transfection (RET) fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as detected by an FDA-approved test.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) by BICR and duration of response (surrogate/intermediate endpoint supporting accelerated approval).

citations.quote: Based on the review of clinical data from Study BLU-667-1101 (ARROW), the clinical and statistical review teams conclude that the Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness of pralsetinib in patients with RET fusion-positive metastatic NSCLC adequate to support accelerated approval.
The confirmed overall response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) in treatment-naïve patients was 70% (95% CI: 50, 86) and the median duration of response was 9.0 months

summary.text: Pralsetinib (a new molecular entity) received Orphan Drug Designation (4/11/2018) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (10/30/2019), and the NDA received priority review. It was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 based on the overall response rate and durability observed in the single-arm ARROW trial, with a required confirmatory report (PMR 3916-1) from the ARROW study to verify clinical benefit.
